model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route) with deal-completes vs deal-breaks scenario weighting
model_label: Live scheme of arrangement (Prologis): base and bull are deal-completes scenarios (one-year horizon, year-1 flow = FY2026E AFFO ~ permitted dividends, exit = the scheme consideration expressed as a multiple of AFFO); bear is the deal-breaks standalone REIT AFFO capitalisation at a GBP cost of equity (FY2026E AFFO capitalised at 8% / 2.5% growth, 17x; net debt NOT deducted because AFFO is post-interest). All three scenarios share a one-year horizon because the engine sizes every scenario from the base.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 statutory revenue per the Metrics CSV (GBP m: gross rental income 637 + JV management fees + other income + trading-property sales). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow that is valued is Adjusted (EPRA) earnings after tax (495 in FY2025 = 68.2% of revenue; 458/675 = 67.9% in FY2024) less spend on existing completed properties (61 in FY2025, 54 in FY2024: refurbishment and fit-out, the maintenance/leasing capex bridge from EPRA earnings to AFFO). Growth on the revenue line is read as adjusted-earnings growth.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,355.3m diluted weighted shares per FY2025 AR note 12 (diluted adjusted EPS 36.5p vs basic 36.6p on 1,352.5m). H1 2026 average basic count 1,352.8m (H1 2026 results presentation footnote 1) implies ~1,355.6m diluted, consistent with the scheme's cash cap (GBP 3.5bn / 1,031.7p = 339m shares = 25% of ~1,357m). Held FLAT: SBC (GBP 5m/yr) is expensed inside adjusted earnings; buybacks (GBP 4m/yr) only fund employee share plans; no raise assumed.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow capitalised is Adjusted (EPRA) earnings less maintenance capex, which is already AFTER net finance costs (FY2025 GBP 94m including JVs at share; H1 2026 GBP 54m) and after tax. Deducting the GBP 4,847m Group net debt at 30-Jun-2026 (GBP 5,919m look-through including JVs at share) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md). total_debt and cash below are the CSV H1-2026 balance-sheet lines, recorded for audit only. LTV 31% SEGRO-only / 32% look-through, net debt:EBITDA 8.3x, average cost of debt 2.8%, 6.3-year average maturity, 84% hedged, GBP 1.5bn cash and undrawn facilities, A-/BBB+ ratings (H1 2026 presentation).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO proxy (GBP m): Adjusted/EPRA earnings after tax 495 less spend on existing completed properties 61 = 434 (32.0p). SEGRO does not publish an AFFO; this is the house bridge. NOT the CSV free_cash_flow of 367 (OCF 396 - PP&E capex 29, which excludes the GBP 473m of development/acquisition spend running through investing activities) and not statutory NPAT 551, which includes GBP 55m of valuation gains. Capitalised development interest (GBP 64m FY2025, c.GBP 70m guided for 2026, reducing thereafter) is left inside adjusted earnings as growth funding, consistent with the GPT.AX treatment, and is listed as a valuation risk.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Adjusted (EPRA) earnings after tax, 36.6p basic / 36.5p diluted, +6.1% on FY2024's 458 (34.5p). H1 2026: 261 (19.3p), +6.5% / +6.6% per share. Statutory profit (FY2025 551; FY2022 -1,927; FY2021 4,060) is dominated by IAS 40 revaluation and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment expense GBP 5m in FY2025 (CSV StockBasedComp; FY2025 AR cash-flow note line 10671) is an IFRS 2 administrative cost expensed INSIDE adjusted/EPRA earnings and not added back, so no second deduction is made; SEGRO's EPRA cost ratio is quoted ex-SBC but the earnings line is not. The share awards it grants are in the diluted count. House and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income (GBP 26m FY2025, mostly interest on cash and JV loans) is left inside adjusted earnings because net debt is not deducted and no cash is added to EV: the matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). fx_rate 100 pence per pound is exact and dateless. The scheme consideration is marked in GBp from USD inputs: PLD USD 129.49 (NYSE close 2026-10-09T20:00Z, Yahoo chart meta, 52-week range 111.03-153.35) and GBPUSD 1.3233 (2026-10-09T21:29Z). Parity check: SEGRO also lists on Euronext Paris, not used.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:35:59Z (LSE regular close; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 632.2-997.4)
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (diluted count, FY2025 AR note 12; H1 2026 results disclose only the 1,352.8m basic average)
inputs.nta_note: EPRA NTA 902p at 30-Jun-2026 (925p Dec-25, 907p Dec-24, 1,137p peak Dec-21), down 2.5% in the half on the incoming UK valuer's higher yields (-1.2% like-for-like valuation). The scheme's 1,031.7p cash alternative is 1.14x this NTA; the 39% premium was to the undisturbed price of c.742p (0.82x NTA). Recorded as a cross-check and as the deal-break reference, not as the valuation: NTA carries the valuers' cap rates, not the house cost of equity.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Two rates, each stated in GBP. (1) Bear / standalone: the GBP COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and no net debt is deducted: UK 10-year gilt ~4.5% + 0.7 beta x 5.0% UK ERP = 8.0%. Cross-check: the undisturbed pre-bid price of c.742p capitalised FY2025 AFFO of 32.0p at a 4.3% yield, i.e. the market's own standalone cost of equity was ~7.0-7.5% for 3% growth, so the house 8.0% sits 0.5-1.0pp above it. (2) Base / bull (deal completes): 8.0% is used as the merger-arbitrage required return on a one-year period. Completion is targeted for H1 2027 (~7-8 months), so a full year at 8% deliberately builds in slippage into H2 2027 (CMA Phase 2 / EC Phase II risk); at the targeted timing the base value would be ~2% higher. The same 8.0% in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the probability weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Head-lease liabilities (GBP 73m at Dec-23, immaterial) are inside adjusted earnings as a GBP 3m/yr interest charge; no separate lease line and no lease liability in the (zero) net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is nil (TotalEquityInclNCI 9,671 vs equity 9,659 in FY2020; nothing since). JV income (SELP and the data-centre JVs) is equity-accounted and already inside adjusted earnings at share.
inputs.notes: Model: live scheme of arrangement, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md 'Live takeover, scheme' row (deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting) with the standalone leg on the REIT row (AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run on the Drivers/engine route per the GPT.AX / CHC.AX precedent: revenue is the driver line, EBITDA margin = adjusted-earnings margin which is post-interest and post-tax so cash_tax_rate = 0, D&A = 0 under IAS 40, SBC = 0 because it is expensed inside the margin, capex = spend on existing completed properties, working capital = 0, net_debt = 0). Deal terms (Analysis JSON, scheme announced 4-Aug-2026, approved by shareholders 28-Sep-2026): 0.0920 new Prologis shares per SEGRO share, plus a cash alternative fixed at 1,031.7p per share for up to 25% of the consideration / GBP 3.5bn, scaled pro rata if over-elected; Prologis declared the proposal 'Best and Final' under Rule 32.2 so terms cannot rise absent a competing bidder. Outstanding: Court sanction, UK CMA, EU Commission, Italian Golden Power, UK NSIA; completion targeted H1 2027. Engine mapping of the deal: base and bull use a ONE-YEAR horizon whose year-1 flow is FY2026E AFFO (460m, 33.9p, which approximates the FY2026 dividends a holder receives before completion: 10.14p interim set 'consistent with the terms of the proposal' plus an assumed ~22p permitted final) and whose exit is the consideration, encoded as terminal_cap_multiple = (consideration + permitted final dividend - year-1 AFFO) / year-1 AFFO so that the cap binds; terminal_growth is set only high enough that Gordon exceeds the cap and carries no economic meaning in those two scenarios. Bear is the standalone AFFO capitalisation on the same one-year horizon (the engine sizes every scenario from the base horizon, so a 10-year bear path cannot sit beside a one-year base): FY2026E AFFO with a 17x exit, which is Gordon at the 8% cost of equity and 2.5% growth. A 10-year component build of the same standalone case (margin 68.2% -> 65.5% as the 2.8% debt book reprices and capitalised interest unwinds, refurbishment spend 8.4% -> 9.0%, growth 6/3/3/3/2.5...%) gives 565p, within 1p of the capitalisation, so nothing is lost by the shorter form. CONSEQUENCE: entry_price, required_return_table and the WACC x g sensitivity grid are derived from the base (deal) flows and are NOT meaningful for this ticker -- they describe a one-year AFFO stream with the cap released at other discount rates. The merger-arbitrage entry price is in deal_analysis. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the 9-Oct-2026 LSE regular close, not an after-hours print. Balance sheet from the 30-Jun-2026 interim (30-Jul-2026); diluted share count from the FY2025 annual report.
warnings: Deal consideration is 75%+ Prologis stock: the base and bull values move ~0.68p per USD 1 move in PLD and ~7p per 0.01 move in GBPUSD; refresh_price.py updates only the SEGRO price, not PLD or FX, so the deal mark goes stale between builds.

The permitted FY2026 final dividend (~22p) is assumed received before completion; if the scheme completes before the final-dividend record date (c.April 2027) or the scheme terms do not permit it, base and bull are ~20p lower.

entry_price, required_return_table and sensitivity are mechanical outputs on a one-year deal scenario and should not be read as a buy-below price or a standalone sensitivity; see deal_analysis for the arbitrage entry price and the bear scenario for the standalone floor.

deal_analysis.structure: UK scheme of arrangement; 0.0920 new PLD shares per SEGRO share; cash alternative 1,031.7p per share for up to 25% of consideration (max GBP 3.5bn), scaled pro rata if over-elected; 'Best and Final' (Rule 32.2) absent a competing offer
deal_analysis.status_as_of: 2026-10-10: shareholder approvals obtained 28-Sep-2026 (Court Meeting and General Meeting); awaiting Court sanction, UK CMA, EU Commission, Italian Golden Power, UK NSIA; completion targeted H1 2027
deal_analysis.blended_formula: 0.75 x 900.3 + 0.25 x 1,031.7: because the cash leg is worth more than the stock leg at current PLD, every rational holder elects cash and the election is scaled to the 25% cap
deal_analysis.expected_completion: H1 2027 target; modelled on a one-year period to absorb Phase 2 regulatory slippage
deal_analysis.deal_break_reference_note: Undisturbed price before the 24-Jun-2026 offer period (39% premium to the 1,031.7p cash alternative implies c.742p, 0.82x NTA). The engine's bear value is the house standalone AFFO value at an 8% cost of equity, which sits well below where the shares last traded pre-bid; both are reported so the reader can pick the break price they believe.
deal_analysis.hurdle_entry_price_note: Price at which collecting 955.1p in one year returns the 15% hurdle with certainty (955.1 / 1.15). Probability-weighted at the scenario weights below it is lower: 0.85 x 830.5 + 0.15 x bear value. This, not entry_price.weighted_entry_price, is the merger-arbitrage buy-below price.
deal_analysis.implied_market_view: Compare current_price with the 884-907p PV of the completed-deal receipts: the market is capitalising the deal at a sub-8% annualised spread with essentially no break probability priced, i.e. it is paying for near-certain completion. A fresh buyer at the current price has 2-4% of upside to the blended consideration and ~35-40% of downside to the house standalone value if the scheme fails.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Adjusted/EPRA EPS, NOT statutory EPS: 31.0p (FY2022) -> 36.6p (FY2025) 3yr; 25.4p (FY2020) -> 36.6p 5yr. Statutory EPS (FY2021 338p, FY2022 -160p, FY2025 41p) is IAS 40 revaluation and its CAGR is meaningless.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Adjusted/EPRA earnings in GBP m: 374 (FY2022) -> 495 (FY2025) 3yr; 292 (FY2020) -> 495 5yr. The AFFO proxy (less spend on existing completed properties) is only reconstructable for FY2024 (404) and FY2025 (434): +7.4% 1yr. Per-share adjusted EPS (5.7% / 7.6%) is the honest organic figure because the 2020 (GBP 672m) and 2024 (GBP 889m) equity raises lifted the GBP totals.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Adjusted EPS record (5.7% 3yr, 7.6% 5yr) and H1 2026 (+6.6%) faded for finance-cost drift as the 2.8% debt book reprices; a 10-year standalone path averages ~3.2% over FY2026-35 and is what the bear's 17x exit multiple encodes. Equity CAGR is not used: NTA is a revaluation series. The deal scenarios do not use a growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (2.6%) diverges from adjusted-earnings 3yr CAGR (9.8%) by more than 30%: the FY2022-23 GBP 2.5bn of IAS 40 write-downs sit in equity, not in earnings. Growth is taken from the adjusted-EPS series.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are distorted by lumpy trading-property sales inside statutory revenue (FY2023 749 vs FY2024 675) and by the 2020 and 2024 equity raises; gross rental income grew 7.6%/yr FY2022-25 (488 -> 637). Adjusted earnings have grown faster than AFFO because spend on existing completed properties rose 13% in FY2025 (54 -> 61).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026E: H1 2026 adjusted earnings +6.5% (261 vs 245), like-for-like NRI +5.3%, GBP 53m of new headline rent contracted; 6% on the revenue driver gives FY2026E adjusted earnings ~525m / 38.7p and AFFO ~460m / 33.9p after 8.4% maintenance spend. This year-1 flow stands in for the FY2026 dividends a holder collects before completion (10.14p interim + ~22p assumed permitted final = ~32p).
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (EPRA) earnings / revenue held at the FY2025 actual 68.2% (FY2024 67.9%). Post net finance costs and post tax.
base.capex_rationale: Spend on existing completed properties (refurbishment and fit-out) at 8.4% of revenue: FY2025 61/726 = 8.4%, FY2024 54/675 = 8.0%. Development and acquisition capex (GBP 500-550m guided for 2026) is growth capital and is not deducted.
base.tax_rationale: Zero because adjusted earnings are already after tax (FY2025 GBP 29m including JVs; H1 2026 GBP 13m). SEGRO is a UK REIT (PID regime) with Continental European subsidiaries that pay local tax inside the line.
base.terminal_note: THE CAP IS THE DEAL. terminal_cap_multiple 27.13x = (blended consideration 933.1p + assumed permitted final dividend 22.0p - year-1 AFFO 33.9p) / 33.9p, so year-1 flow plus exit = 955.1p of receipts and the scenario value is 955.1p / 1.08 = ~884p. terminal_growth 4.5% has no economic meaning here: it is set only so that Gordon at 8% (29.9x) exceeds the cap and the cap binds. The consideration itself is 27.5x FY2026E AFFO / 24.1x FY2026E adjusted EPS / 1.03x NTA (1.14x on the cash leg).

bull.growth_rationale: Same FY2026E flow as base; the bull axis is the consideration, not SEGRO's operations.
bull.terminal_note: THE CAP IS THE DEAL AT A RECOVERED PLD PRICE. PLD back to USD 145 (its level when the 0.0920 ratio was struck at parity with the 1,031.7p cash in July 2026; 52-week high 153.35) at GBPUSD 1.3233 makes the stock leg 1,008.1p and the blended consideration 1,014.0p; plus 22.0p permitted final dividend = 1,036.0p of receipts; cap = (1,036.0 - 33.9) / 33.9 = 29.52x; value = 1,036.0 / 1.08 = ~959p. A competing bid at ~1,030-1,050p (the only route to higher terms under Rule 32.2) lands in the same place. Gordon at 8% / 4.5% = 29.9x just exceeds the cap so the cap binds.

bear.growth_rationale: DEAL BREAKS (regulatory block, Court refusal or a Prologis walk-away on a MAC) in 2027 and SEGRO reverts to standalone. FY2026 is largely banked (+6%: H1 adjusted earnings +6.5%, like-for-like NRI +5.3%), giving FY2026E adjusted earnings ~525m / 38.7p and AFFO ~460m / 33.9p. Beyond FY2026 the standalone path (FY2027-29 at 3% as deal costs and a year of subordinated strategy bite, then 2.5% from indexed/reviewed rent, 12% reversion and GBP 90m of pipeline rent, against 1-2% annual disposals) is carried in the exit multiple, not in explicit years, because the engine holds every scenario to the base horizon.
bear.margin_rationale: FY2026E adjusted-earnings margin at the FY2025 actual 68.2%. The standalone drift to ~65.5% over five years (GBP 6.3bn of look-through debt at 2.8% repricing toward 4%+ as hedges and bonds roll; c.GBP 70m/yr of capitalised development interest unwinding into the P&L as projects complete; partly offset by the <18% cost ratio) is what the 17x exit, rather than the ~22x pre-bid market multiple, is pricing.
bear.capex_rationale: Refurbishment and fit-out spend at 8.4% of revenue (FY2025 61/726). Standalone it drifts to ~9% as the older West London estates and 1990s big boxes are refurbished for occupancy and EPC compliance; that drift is inside the exit multiple.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0% / 2.5% = 17.1x FY2026E AFFO (a 5.9% AFFO yield) sits a hair above the 17x cap, so the cap binds at 17x: value = (33.9p + 17 x 33.9p) / 1.08 = ~566p, 0.63x the 902p EPRA NTA. Cross-check: a 10-year component build of the same standalone case (growth 6/3/3/3/2.5x6 %, margin 68.2 -> 65.5%, capex 8.4 -> 9.0%, 17x exit on year-10 AFFO of ~41p) gives 565p. Pre-bid SEGRO traded at ~22x AFFO (4.3% yield, ~7% implied cost of equity); 17x is where a standalone SEGRO sits at the house 8%.

scenario_narratives.base: The Prologis scheme completes on its agreed terms during 2027 after Court sanction and the four regulatory clearances (UK CMA, EU Commission, Italian Golden Power, UK NSIA). Every holder elects the 1,031.7p cash alternative, it is scaled to the 25% cap, and the remaining 75% is settled in 0.0920 PLD shares marked at the last PLD close and GBPUSD rate (933.1p blended); the FY2026 interim and a permitted ~22p final dividend are collected on the way. Discounted a full year at an 8% merger-arbitrage required return to absorb Phase 2 slippage, the receipts are worth ~884p today (~907p at the targeted H1 2027 timing). SEGRO's own FY2026 operations (adjusted earnings +6%, AFFO ~34p) matter only as the dividend stream and as the floor under the stock.
scenario_narratives.bull: The deal completes and the stock leg is worth more at completion than today: PLD recovers to ~USD 145, where the exchange ratio was struck at parity with the cash in July 2026 (52-week high USD 153), or sterling weakens, lifting the blended consideration to ~1,014p; plus the permitted final dividend, ~1,036p of receipts worth ~959p today. A competing bid is the alternative route to the same number: Prologis's 'Best and Final' statement caps its own terms, and the GBP 14bn size and pan-European antitrust footprint make an interloper (Blackstone, GIC, Goodman) unlikely but not impossible. There is no bull case for SEGRO's own operations inside a one-year horizon.
scenario_narratives.bear: The scheme fails: a regulatory block or remedy package Prologis will not accept, a Court refusal, or a walk-away on a material adverse change in a stressed market. SEGRO reverts to standalone with a year of subordinated strategy and deal costs behind it, the Prologis-funded acceleration of the GBP 1.6bn land bank and 2.5GW data-centre pipeline is gone, and the shares re-rate from a deal multiple back to an income multiple. FY2026 adjusted earnings still grow ~6% (banked), AFFO ~34p; thereafter 2.5-3% growth as indexed rent and reversion capture are offset by a 2.8% debt book repricing toward 4%+ and capitalised interest unwinding, with refurbishment spend edging up to 9% of revenue -- all of which the 17x exit prices. Capitalised at an 8% GBP cost of equity, the standalone AFFO stream is worth ~566p, about 0.63x the 902p EPRA NTA and well below the ~742p undisturbed price. The market would probably stop nearer the undisturbed level than the house value on day one, but the house value is the number a fresh buyer should underwrite.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: The three-scenario frame is replaced by deal-completes (85%) vs deal-breaks (15%), per the dcf-methods routing row for live schemes. 15% break: shareholder approval is already in hand, Prologis is an A-rated acquirer paying mostly in its own stock with no financing condition and a declared strategic rationale, but four regulatory reviews remain (CMA scrutiny of localised UK warehouse overlaps and NSIA review of the Slough data-centre cluster are the live ones), the timetable runs to H1 2027, and the base rate for recommended, approved GBP 10bn+ cross-border schemes failing on regulatory or MAC grounds is high-single-digit to mid-teens. The 85% completes is split 65/20 between the consideration at the current PLD mark (base) and a PLD recovery or competing bid (bull): PLD sits in the lower third of its 52-week range and a 12% recovery by completion is plausible but no more likely than a further fall, which the base, marked at the current price, already carries as its expected value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SEGRO is valued as a merger-arbitrage position, not as a going-concern REIT, because a shareholder-approved Prologis scheme sets the near-term outcome. Base and bull are the scheme receipts (blended stock-plus-capped-cash consideration plus permitted dividends) discounted at an 8% arbitrage return over a year; bear is the standalone business valued the house way for a REIT -- adjusted (EPRA) earnings less refurbishment spend, i.e. AFFO, capitalised at an 8% GBP cost of equity with no net-debt deduction because the flow is post-interest. Statutory earnings, book-value growth and reported free cash flow are set aside as IAS 40 revaluation noise and development-capex timing. The finding is that the price already embeds near-certain completion: the probability-weighted value lands below the price because a 15% break probability against a ~40% fall to the house standalone value outweighs a 2-4% spread to the consideration. The investment question is therefore not SEGRO's intrinsic value but whether a sub-8% annualised, 85%-probability arbitrage with that asymmetry is worth holding; for a new buyer it is not, and for an existing holder the case for selling into the spread is strong unless they want to own Prologis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Consideration mark: 75% of the deal value is PLD stock. Each USD 1 on PLD moves the base ~0.68p (~0.7%); a 10% PLD fall to USD 116 takes the blended consideration to ~866p, below the current price. refresh_price.py does not refresh PLD or GBPUSD.

Break probability and break price: the weighted value is most sensitive to the 15% break weight and to whether the break price is the house standalone (~565p) or the undisturbed level (~742p); at 742p the weighted value rises ~27p.
Timing: each extra quarter of regulatory delay costs ~2% of the base value at an 8% arbitrage rate; CMA Phase 2 or EC Phase II would push completion into H2 2027.
Permitted dividends: the ~22p FY2026 final is assumed received; completion before the record date or a stricter scheme term removes it (~2% of base).

Standalone floor: the bear capitalises FY2026E AFFO at 8% with a 17x exit; at the market's own ~7% pre-bid cost of equity the standalone value is ~700p, so the floor is itself a judgment, and capitalised development interest (c.GBP 70m/yr) left inside adjusted earnings flatters it by ~5p/share of AFFO.

data_sources.financials: SGRO.L Metrics CSV / core_metrics and kpis (adjusted/EPRA earnings and EPS, EPRA NTA, LTV, gross and net rental income, dividends, share counts) adjudicated from the FY2021-FY2025 annual reports and the H1 2026 results presentation (30-Jul-2026: adjusted income statement, net debt, LTV, cost of debt, EBITDA), the 8-Jul-2026 H1 trading update (905p pro forma NAV, capex guidance) and the H1 2026 property analysis report. FY2025 AR: adjusted earnings table and diluted share count (lines 10465-10482), capital expenditure paragraph with spend on existing completed properties and capitalised interest (lines 2884-2900), net debt table (lines 10592-10606).
